$comment: What may claim to be a TCAP-FIELD-TESTABLE item, and on whose authority. Sean Reynolds, first pass over FORM-A, 2026-09-03: 'this is a mixed classroom assessment, not a TCAP-field-testable form.' A form that mixes twelve selected-response items with six extended responses reads as a test form and is not one. The distinction now travels WITH the item.
sourceOfRecord: Sean Reynolds (TN Level 5 U.S. History teacher), 2026-09-03
notTdoe: This is NOT a TDOE publication. TDOE has issued no 2027-28 item specification, so nothing here may be described as a state requirement. When a state spec is published, replace this file and re-measure every item against it — do not amend it in place.
defaultRationale: tcapFormat is FALSE until something affirms it. An unaffirmed claim of field-testability is exactly the kind of compliance claim that must never be made by default, and a boolean that defaults to true is a claim nobody made.

neverTcapFormat.why: An extended response and a document-based question are instructionally valuable and are not selected-response items. Sean: they 'must be tagged tcap_format: false and supported by rubrics.'

requiredBeforeTrue.why: Sean, same pass: the selected-response items 'lack the required standards, DOK/Hess, distractor, bias, citation, and IRT metadata.' An item missing any of these cannot be judged field-testable, so it cannot claim to be.

fieldNameNote: Sean wrote tcap_format. The record is camelCase throughout (dokLevel, standardCodes, irtParameters), so the field is tcapFormat. Say the word if you want the snake_case spelling instead — it is one rename plus a gate string.
